items.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: [(note)] Monk Rowe also participated briefly in the interview.

ctx.x: Claude “Fiddler” Williams was born in Muskogee, Oklahoma in 1908. As a child he was surrounded by music and learned mandolin, guitar and violin. He received his first on-the-job training playing with the Black road shows that traveled across the southwest. Gigs with Andy Kirk’s Twelve Clouds of Joy and bands in the hot jazz atmosphere of Kansas City honed his skills and Claude traveled with Count Basie’s first swing band in 1936. His career has included work with rhythm & blues groups, collaborations with Jay…
Claude was interviewed by Michael Woods on September 4, 1995, in Los Angeles. Monk Rowe also participated briefly in the interview.
We are filming a interview for the Hamilton Jazz Archive with our guest today, Claude Williams, virtuoso violinist. Pleased to meet you.
